about: GENERATED by tools/spec-tree.js from the government documents (sources/, tools/spec-read.js) and sources/hand-science.json — never edit by hand (a hand edit fails the build). A node per heading and per statement, named as printed. THE @FAMILY SCIENCE TOPIC TREE, FROM THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN LISTS (owner, 25 Nov), in the one format of data/settings/curriculum/uk/maths.json (tools/lib/curriculum.js): subject › topic › sub-topic, each node an id, a short plain name (paraphrased), its `src` lines (the DfE document and its section heading exactly as printed, one of headings.json: the GCSE topic – sub-heading, the National Curriculum year and topic) and, for a sub-topic, its levels (KS1, KS2, KS3; GCSE Combined = in the combined science content and so in the single sciences too; GCSE Separate = in the single-science content only). Higher-only content is underlined in the DfE documents and cannot be read from their text, so no level says Higher. A science question's `dfe` is read from this table only: `ideas` (its sci-ideas idea, an AQA spec point), `spec` (its AQA 8461/2/3/4 `spec_ref` point, the longest section prefix listed), `set`, `topic` (a source topic name). An A-Level set is outside these documents. Checked by tools/one-curriculum.js; `budget` (questions with no node) may only fall.
